stimulus.body: 문장: 어제 책을 읽____ 친구에게 얘기했어요.

questions.stem: Which option correctly fills the blank marked gieut?

options.text: 고, because the two actions happened in sequence
아서, because reading caused the telling
options.misconception: uses a causal connective where no cause is stated

options.text: 지만, because the actions contrast
options.misconception: uses the contrastive connective for sequential events

options.text: 기, because the reading is nominalized
options.misconception: uses the nominalizing form where a clause link is needed

questions.explanation: Reading the book and telling the friend are two actions in sequence, so the connective 고 is appropriate. 아서 would assert that reading caused the telling, 지만 would introduce a contrast, and 기 would nominalize the verb instead of linking clauses.
questions.hint: Two actions in order take the sequential connective.

questions.stem: Which option correctly fills the blank marked ass-eo?

options.text: 갔어요, because the time word 어제 calls for the past tense
가요, because the event is habitual
options.misconception: uses the present tense for a specific past event

options.text: 갈 거예요, because the event is planned
options.misconception: uses the future tense where a past event is reported

options.text: 가고 있어요, because the action is ongoing
options.misconception: uses the progressive form for a finished event

questions.explanation: The adverb 어제 fixes the event in the past, so the past tense 갔어요 is required. 가요 is present, 갈 거예요 is a future plan, and 가고 있어요 describes an action in progress, all of which conflict with a completed event yesterday.
questions.hint: 어제 requires a past-tense verb ending.

stimulus.body: 문장: 저는 매일 아침 운동____ 사람이에요.

questions.stem: Which option correctly fills the blank marked neun?

options.text: 하는, because the modifier describes a person who exercises
한, because the exercising is finished
options.misconception: uses a past adnominal where a general habit is described

options.text: 할, because the person will exercise later
options.misconception: uses a future modifier for a habitual behavior

options.text: 하고, because two actions are listed
options.misconception: uses a clause connective where a noun modifier is needed

questions.hint: A noun modifier for a habitual action uses the present adnominal.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize and apply geu in Korean language and culture contexts
questions.stem: Which option correctly fills the blank marked geu?

options.text: 어요, because the stem ends in a vowel and the sentence is polite
아요, because any adjective takes 아요
options.misconception: uses the wrong vowel-form ending for this stem

options.text: 습니다, because the stem ends in a consonant
options.misconception: uses the formal ending with the wrong stem assumption

options.text: 네요, because the speaker is surprised
options.misconception: uses an exclamatory ending where a plain polite statement is needed

questions.explanation: 재미있다 has a stem ending in a vowel sound, so the polite present form is 재미있어요. 아요 is used after consonant stems, 습니다 is a different speech level, and 네요 adds a nuance of surprise not present in the statement.
questions.hint: Check the final sound of the stem before choosing the polite ending.
